constraints.name: Automated decision-making on expense claims
constraints.rationale_summary: Whether auto-approving a sub-£50 claim with no human review triggers Article 22 protections is genuinely contested here.
constraints.reasoning: This is the case instructions.md reserves for requires_legal_review: no precedented mitigation pattern exists because the underlying legal question (does this threshold-based auto-approval trigger Article 22) is itself unresolved, not just the mitigation.

constraints.name: Employee data protection
constraints.rationale_summary: Standard obligation for any system processing employee personal/financial data — not novel, not a blocker on its own.
constraints.reasoning: Same baseline classification as in the typical example — routine, not contested.

constraints.name: Financial record retention
constraints.rationale_summary: Auto-approved claims are still accounting records requiring statutory retention; the approval path does not change the duty.
constraints.mitigation_summary: Retain the auto-approval decision record alongside the claim for the statutory period, exportable for audit.
constraints.reasoning: Swept as an ongoing duty per the scenario rules: automating the approval removes the manager's record, so the retention design must capture the automated decision itself.

overall_status.rationale_summary: CON-01 is Red with only a legal-review flag, not a mitigation — the underlying legal question is itself unresolved, so no discount applies.

components.name: regulatory_posture
components.reasoning: CON-01 is Red and requires legal review, placing the component in the 0-3 band on severity alone; lifted to 5.0 only because the other two constraints are clean and CON-03 carries a concrete mitigation.

components.name: idea_clarity
components.reasoning: The brief is unusually precise: a named threshold, a named mechanism, and a bounded internal scope. Clarity is high even though the regulatory answer is not.
